本节练习与排位结束后，这位意大利车手透露自己状态并非最佳，他仍在从一场疾病中恢复，这场病导致他缺席了周四的媒体职责。
他告诉天空体育F1频道：“说实话，这个周末并不轻松。”
“肯定还是没恢复到百分之百。外界在谈论（总冠军争夺）可能发生什么，我确实比平时更紧张一些。”
“确实，我感觉没那么放松，但我会尽量今晚睡个好觉，把注意力放在明天。”
基米·安东内利即将成为一级方程式史上最年轻的世界冠军，泰德·克拉维茨回顾了此前打破这一纪录的车手们的历史
尽管身体状况不佳，安东内利在排位赛中仍跑出了相当不错的最后一圈，与杆位得主刘易斯·汉密尔顿的差距在零点二秒以内。
然而，他的队友乔治·拉塞尔仅以微弱差距落后汉密尔顿位列第二，这或许反映出这位意大利车手未能发挥出自己的最佳水平。
安东内利补充道：“我在Q3中很难从轮胎上找到好的感觉。我就是没有最大的信心。我有点紧张，不骗你。”
“那一圈跑得很差，到处都有很多失误。总的来说，仍然是第四名，明天还有很多可以争取的。”
基米·安东内利承认，在墨西哥城大奖赛仅排位第五后，他感到“有点紧张”
“太疯狂了！”——诺里斯乐于把第一名让给安东内利
兰多·诺里斯表示，当梅赛德斯车手安东内利取代他成为世界冠军时，他“非常乐意”将今年迈凯伦赛车上的1号让给安东内利。
安东内利在仅仅第二个F1赛季中就大幅超出预期，全面压倒了年初还是明显夺冠热门的拉塞尔。
“他做得非常出色，而且是以相当惊人的方式做到的，”诺里斯在墨西哥比赛周末前说道。
“人们说今年他没有遇到任何强劲的竞争。这恰恰证明了他做得如此出色。
他有一位非常非常有天赋的队友，而他在整个赛季中都击败了这位队友。
随着梅赛德斯的基米·安东内利接近锁定2026年F1世界冠军，其他车手对这位意大利人的赛季表现发表了看法
“我对基米只有尊重。他是个非常好的人。我们相处得非常好，我非常乐意把1号车让给他。
“他配得上。他做得非常出色，尤其是在他进入一级方程式的第二年。最年轻的世界冠军，这相当疯狂。
“我喜欢看到别人取得那样的成功。看到这样的情景真好。”

detailEn: Kimi Antonelli: Mercedes driver admits to feeling 'tense' amid effort to seal F1 title at Mexico City Grand Prix

Kimi Antonelli needs top-nine finish to become world champion at Mexico City Grand Prix; he only qualified fifth and was off the pace compared to Mercedes team-mate George Russell; watch Sunday's race at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1
Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix
Kimi Antonelli has admitted to feeling "more tense than usual" ahead of attempting to seal the Formula 1 world championship at Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix.
The 20-year-old only needs to finish ninth in the race to become the sport's youngest world champion.
Antonelli qualified fifth on Saturday but will start from fourth on the grid due to a penalty for Max Verstappen.

Speaking after the session, the Italian revealed that he is not feeling his best as he continues to recover from an illness that caused him to miss his media duties on Thursday.
He told Sky Sports F1: "It has not been the easiest weekend to be fair.
"Definitely still not feeling 100 per cent. There is talk of what could happen [with the championship] and definitely I'm a bit more tense than usual.
"Definitely I don't feel as relaxed but I try to have a good sleep tonight and focus on tomorrow."
With Kimi Antonelli on the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest ever world champion, Ted Kravitz looks at the history of those who have broken that record previously
Despite his condition, Antonelli was still able to produce a decent final lap in qualifying as he finished within two tenths of pole-sitter Lewis Hamilton.
However, the fact that his team-mate George Russell was only marginally behind Hamilton in second perhaps reflected the Italian not being able to summon his best level.
Antonelli added: "I struggled to get a good feeling from the tyres in Q3. I just didn't have the most confidence. I was a bit tense, I am not going to lie.
"It was a poor lap, many mistakes here and there. Overall, still P4 and a lot to play for tomorrow."
Kimi Antonelli admits he felt 'a bit tense' after qualifying only fifth for the Mexico City Grand Prix
'It's insane!' - Norris happy to pass No 1 onto Antonelli
Lando Norris says he is "more than happy" to pass the number one he has had on his McLaren this year to Antonelli when the Mercedes driver replaces him as world champion.
Antonelli has massively exceeded expectations during just his second season in F1 to comprehensively outperform Russell, who began the year as the clear title favourite.
"He's done an incredible job and done it in a pretty incredible way," Norris said ahead of the race weekend in Mexico.
"People are saying he hasn't had any tough competition this year. That proves the point that he's done such an incredible job.
"He's got a very, very talented team-mate that he's beaten through the whole season.
As Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli nears clinching the 2026 F1 championship, the rest of the grid give their verdict on the Italian's season
"I have nothing but respect for Kimi. He's a very nice guy. We get along very well and I'm more than happy to pass the No 1 over to him.
"He deserves it. He's done an incredible job, especially in his second year in Formula 1. Youngest world champion, it's pretty insane.
"I enjoy other people having that kind of success. It's nice to see."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
